quest.title: The Palace, Dyed in Black
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

chapter.num: True Tales of the Violet Garden: Act IV
chapter.title: The Palace, Dyed in Black

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Ah, you're here. It appears everyone has arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How did your investigation go, Kazuha?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Last night I visited a former servant who once worked for my family. I was able to learn the entirety of what happened all those years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: In my great-grandfather's generation, the Isshin Art was tasked with forging an important Goshintou according to an ancient forging diagram.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Though all the craftsmen involved were very experienced, the process was still unsuccessful. Every blade that was forged was defective.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: When the deadline came, the blade still wasn't finished, so the craftsmen all fled and hid for fear of punishment.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: The Kaedehara Clan and Yashiro Commission then conducted an investigation. My great-grandfather and the head of the Kamisato Clan eventually tracked down the craftsmen near the seaside.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: However, they met fierce resistance from the craftsmen, and in the end, they were unable to prevent them from escaping by sea.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: The Kaedehara Clan was severely punished for the swordsmiths that had escaped, and the family gradually fell into decline.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Moreover, I heard that the head of the Kamisato Clan was injured by the fleeing swordsmiths, which, combined with his advanced age, caused him to pass away shortly thereafter.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Yes... The sudden passing of the family head left the Kamisato Clan leaderless. Treacherous people took advantage of the situation and put the family's status in the Yashiro Commission at jeopardy.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: This single incident had profound effects. Even after the position as head of the clan was passed to my father, the Kamisato Clan still wasn't able to regain its prior reputation.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I see...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: But, thanks to my brother, everything is getting better now.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: The failure to forge the blade was ultimately attributed to a lack of required skill and finesse. The Kaedehara Clan and the Yashiro Commission always believed that was the case.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: However, the story of The Five Kasen seems to imply that the failure didn't stem from a lack of skill, but rather, the diagram had been tampered with by someone.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Miss Kamisato, I heard yesterday that the Yashiro Commission has still kept the diagram ever since the failed forging all those years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Might I ask you to do me a favor?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Yes, I understand. I will go back and search for the diagram. Please come meet me at the Kamisato Estate later.

talks.objective: Go to The Five Kasen Plaza

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Everyone, I've managed to find the old diagram.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hmm. Though the diagram is well-preserved, you can still tell that it's seen at least three or four centuries of history.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, that's pretty old! Is it still possible to find any evidence of tampering?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: At this point, we can only try our luck and see how we fare.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: They immerse the diagram into a basin of water, and after a short while...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Although the effect is not too obvious, you can still see that some words have now started to smudge.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Kazuha, this is clear evidence that this chart was indeed tampered with. Someone framed the Kaedehara Clan all those years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: *sigh* I see, but I fear that I've discovered this secret too late...

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: When my grandfather was young, he proposed reviving the Isshin Art many times to my great-grandfather. But my grandfather was only scolded for being too foolhardy.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Yesterday, the former family servant said that my great-grandfather even went to the Yashiro Commission to request that diagram from the head of the Kamisato Clan. He then showed that diagram to my grandfather and asked him and his subordinates to try to forge the sword.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Sure enough, my grandfather also failed. My great-grandfather then told him, "If you can't find the secret within, then the Isshin Art deserves to fade from the world."

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: My grandfather left Inazuma in a rage after hearing those words. He didn't ever see my great-grandfather again, even till the day of his passing.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Looking back at it now, the argument between the two of them was simply... meaningless.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Kazuha...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I heard that your great-grandfather was very industrious when he was young. But later in life, he no longer bothered with the forging arts. It appears that his failure took quite a toll on him.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Kazuha, did your great-grandfather really say "if you can't find the secret within"? Did he use those exact words?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Yes, the servant said that he personally heard those words and still remembers them very clearly.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: My grandfather was so angry at the time that he smashed my great-grandfather's cherished bonsai tree...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait, Albedo. Are you trying to say...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: #Yes, it appears that you understand my meaning, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Kazuha, if your great-grandfather thought that the Isshin Art lacked finesse, then after witnessing his son's failure, wouldn't he have said something more along the lines of "your skills aren't sufficient"?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: But instead he said, "If you can't find the secret within." Don't you find that a little strange?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh!

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: So, you're saying... my great-grandfather may have very well known that the failure was due to someone's tampering?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Yes, the current evidence suggests that it is highly likely.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I apologize, but would you all please accompany me to the Tenryou Commission?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: After I became a wanted criminal, the Tenryou Commission seized my family's last remaining estate, which contained all of my family's old belongings.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I want to inquire about the whereabouts of those belongings. If I can find them, we might be able to get some clues.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, let's get moving!

dialogues.speaker: Asakawa
dialogues.text: You must be here to investigate the Kaedehara Clan's belongings. Madam Kujou has already informed me of the situation. Please, come this way.

talks.objective: Go to the Tenryou Commission Headquarters

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: This flowerpot was in my house for a long time. I heard that it was left behind by my great-grandfather.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, the plants seem to have been dead for a while now.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Well, after my great-grandfather stopped studying the forging arts, he picked up the hobby of keeping bonsai plants. Most of his prized plants were given to others once he became seriously ill.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: But he specifically left behind this dead plant at the time, and even instructed my grandfather not to throw it away in his will.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: My grandfather deeply regretted that he never managed to reconcile with my great-grandfather, so he left the plant exactly as it was.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: But now that I think about it, my great-grandfather could very well have left it behind for other reasons.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, now that you mention it, this flower pot is kinda suspicious.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Yes. Let's take a closer look, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: They find a hidden compartment at the bottom of the flowerpot...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We finally found something! Huh, it's only a bunch of blank paper.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you think someone already discovered the compartment and swapped the contents?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: No, I do not think that is the case here. See the paper? It's quite yellowed, which means it's very old.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe we need to try using water again.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Hmm. You mean to say that these sheets have been written with special ink, like that which Miss Kamisato found before?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Yes, I agree with this hypothesis.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, let's give it a dunk then!

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: There is a pond outside the Police Station. I'll use the water there.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Hmm? What are you all doing here? Did something happen on Ritou?

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Kujou Sara, perhaps you still remember me?

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Yes, I do. You're Kaedehara Kazuha, a wanted criminal during the Vision Hunt Decree. However, your arrest warrant has since been repealed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sara, we'd like to ask about the Kaedehara Clan's property that was seized by the Tenryou Commission. Do you know where all their belongings are now?

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Yes, the items seized at that time are currently stored in the warehouse next to the Police Station. Since Kaedehara has come back to Inazuma, those items should be returned to their rightful owner.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: No, I'm afraid you misunderstand. I'm not here to reclaim those belongings. I just want to investigate them for a personal matter.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: I see. Alright, I'll inform the Police Station. They'll take you into the warehouse.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thank you, Sara!

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Ahem... Kaedehara, about the Vision Hunt Decree...

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: That's all in the past now, Kujou Sara. There's no need to mention it again. I know you've also had your own convictions and struggles.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: However, may I ask something of you?

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Yes, what is it?

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Currently, I have no plans to stay in Inazuma. As a result, those items from my family's estate are of no use to me.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Madam Kujou, I believe you're a person of integrity. After our investigation is over, I'd like to ask if you can handle those belongings for me. Please, sell them and use the money to help the poor.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Alright, I understand. I'll be sure to take care of it.

choices.text: We're just here to ask about something.

talks.objective: Go to the Police Station warehouse

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Yoshinori
dialogues.text: ...It was night, and after the clues led us down to shore, I waited for the culprits to show themselves. However, there were no swordsmiths in sight, only a single eccentric stranger.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Yoshinori
dialogues.text: This stranger claimed to be the one behind the failed forgings and said that he had been patiently waiting for us. He then threatened to destroy the Raiden Gokaden.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Yoshinori
dialogues.text: That person was of able body, and in a blink of an eye, myself and the accompanying samurai had been defeated.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Yoshinori
dialogues.text: Commissioner Kamisato was severely wounded, and I barely escaped death myself. My hat had fortunately blunted a blow to my head.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Yoshinori
dialogues.text: The unusual stranger could've easily claimed my life at that moment. But, after noticing my appearance, he stopped his attacks, and sternly asked if I had any connection with the name "Niwa."

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Yoshinori
dialogues.text: I answered that it was my father's surname and after my father disappeared, I was adopted by the Kaedehara family.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Yoshinori
dialogues.text: Upon hearing my answer, the stranger paused. After a long silence, he suddenly said: "Tell her this. My name is Kunikuzushi." He then turned and left...

talks.objective: Examine the old items belonging to the Kaedehara Clan

dialogues.speaker: Asakawa
dialogues.text: The Kaedehara Clan's belongings are stored in this warehouse. Unfortunately, the items are scattered throughout in order to save space. My deepest apologies.

dialogues.speaker: Asakawa
dialogues.text: However, I have clearly marked the corresponding items, so they shouldn't be too difficult to find.

dialogues.speaker: Asakawa
dialogues.text: I'll be waiting for you at the door, please come see me if you require any assistance.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Kazuha, since the items are scattered throughout the building, I propose we split up and look for clues.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Yes, sounds like a plan. Thanks for your help, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hmm, there must be some around here somewhere...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you looking for, Venti?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Do you see all these pots here? Some of them are bound to have liquor inside, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Everyone else is trying hard to help and you're over here looking for a drink!?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Haha, I merely jest, of course. C'mon, we're close to uncovering the truth now, why do you look so worried?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, Paimon doesn't really get why Kazuha told Sara to sell all these belongings...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What if we don't end up finding anything today? Then wouldn't Kazuha lose the chance of finding out what really happened all those years ago? ...Y'know, just saying.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I know you are worried about Kazuha, but if you ask me, he is stronger than you think.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Since Kazuha made such a request to Sara, that indicates he's already made his choice. Whether we find out the truth or not today, or whatever it turns out to be, he's ready to accept it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is this your archon's intuition speaking?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: No, not intuition. Rather, I've lived for a long time now, so you could say I have some experience in reading people.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Leave the things here to me, you two can look around elsewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ayaka, how's it going for you?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: #Oh, it's you, {NICKNAME}. I'm currently investigating this sword rack.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, since the Kaedehara Clan was a family of renowned swordsmiths, then this blade should be super valuable, right? *gasp* Maybe it's a treasure of the Isshin Art!?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I'm afraid not. Although the sword rack is made of fine wood, the swords placed here appear to be quite ordinary. Due to the dire financial situation of the late Kaedehara Clan, everything of value has probably been sold off already.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: The blade on this sword hasn't been sharpened, but there are many signs of use on the hilt. Perhaps Kaedehara used it for training as a child.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let Paimon see... Oh, there seems to be a couple uneven characters etched into the scabbard! "Kazu"... "ha." Wow, so it really was Kazuha's!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can imagine what Kazuha was like as a kid, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I will continue investigating here and call you if I find anything interesting.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What did you find, Xingqiu?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: I've found quite the pile of old books.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: These books here are all related to smelting steel, and these are about the process of forging blades. This pile over here is all about plants and flowers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, the books about plants and flowers must have belonged to Kazuha's great-grandfather.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could there be any clues in the books?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: I skimmed through them just now, but I didn't find anything particularly worth noting. I shall take a closer look and let you know if I find anything.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you. Unfortunately, I have yet to find anything of value here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, this folding screen looks pretty old, though.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Yes. Perhaps if it were better maintained, then it could fetch a decent price. However, I doubt it could be sold in its current condition.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I was taking a closer look just now and noticed a large piece of dirt caught in the fabric fibers on the backside.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The soil is deeply embedded into the cloth. That means a great deal of force was used when the dirt was lodged into the cloth. It's likely that this patch of dirt is from the very flower pot thrown by Kazuha's grandfather.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Because this is not what we are looking for now.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Let me think... If I wanted to leave a message behind, I would probably choose to leave it on something a little more special. Hmm...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Albedo seems to be thinking pretty hard, we'd better not bother him.

choices.text: Why don't you think this is of any value?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well? How did it go? Those weren't just plain old sheets of paper, were they?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Just as everyone guessed, after I sprinkled some water onto the paper, writing did indeed begin to appear on it. It is a letter written by my great-grandfather.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, what does the letter say?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is it something you can share with us, too?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: It is. I'll tell you what my great-grandfather knew at the time. But before that, I wish to take you somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Everyone, please follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, so that's what really happened!

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Yes. My great-grandfather and the head of the Kamisato Clan escaped from death and learned that the forging diagram had been tampered with by Kunikuzushi.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: However, due to the encounter, the head of the Kamisato Clan was worried that my great-grandfather would be falsely accused of being involved with the perpetrator. So even on his deathbed, the master of the Kamisato Clan cautioned my great-grandfather to never speak of what happened.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Because the perpetrator said he would destroy the Raiden Gokaden, my great-grandfather worried that the perpetrator would still return for vengeance. So, to protect his loved ones, he closed the family business.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: He said: "As the leader of the Kaedehara Clan, I am deeply ashamed to witness the decline of the Isshin Art. But, as a father, it is my priority to ensure the safety of my children and grandchildren."

choices.text: So all those harsh words he said...

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Yes, that's right. If my grandpa had somehow discovered the secret behind the tampered diagram all those years ago, perhaps my great-grandfather would've told him the truth.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Unfortunately, he failed to catch any of the hints in my great-grandfather's words.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Miss Kamisato, it appears you were unaware of the happenings that my great-grandfather described here. What are your thoughts?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Hmm, I suppose the reason the head of the Kamisato House never spoke of this to the family was due to similar safety concerns.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: If the perpetrator was capable of tampering with even the Shogun's diagrams, and could single-handedly defeat many men, then he is not an ordinary enemy.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: I will discuss this matter with brother shortly and investigate the identity behind the one called "Kunikuzushi." Rest assured, we will act cautiously.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How are you feeling, Kazuha?

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: To be honest, as I read the letter, I felt much turbulence in my heart. But now, I've managed to calm myself.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: My great-grandfather said in the letter that he did not wish his descendants to blindly seek revenge and be deceived by things of the past.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Though he was in a tight situation when he wrote these words, I feel like they are still valid nonetheless.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: I think what's most important for each person is not the past, but the present. Even though we must carry the burdens from the past, there are also things we wish to strive for.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Therefore, knowing the truth behind what happened is enough for me. I will live on just as my great-grandfather had hoped.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: That being said, if the enemy from all those years ago is still lurking and plotting to stir up more trouble, then I definitely won't turn a blind eye.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: These are simply insights I've gathered from all that I've experienced.

response.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
response.text: Thank you all for accompanying me in my search for the truth behind that incident.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great! Now that we're done here, let's head back to Ritou.

choices.text: Were because he was worried about his son's well-being.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Kaedehara, why did you lead us to this beach?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is this place related to the contents of the letter?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: It is... In fact, my great-grandfather and the head of the Kamisato Clan tracked the fleeing swordsmiths to this very location.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Our hypothesis was correct. My great-grandfather was well aware of the truth behind the defective blades. And it was right here where they encountered the culprit who framed the Kaedehara Clan and the Raiden Gokaden.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: It reads:

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: "To whoever reads this letter: I, Kaedehara Yoshinori, have been held to a certain secret throughout my entire life. I don't have much longer in this world, and after much consideration, I've finally decided to disclose the matter."

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: "All those years ago, when I was pursuing the swordsmiths alongside Commissioner Kamisato of the Yashiro Commission, I was not injured by one of the fleeing smiths. Rather..."

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: I've already informed the Police Station. There'll be someone to take you into the warehouse, so you may head there directly.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: As for all the belongings left by the Kaedehara Clan, I will deal with them promptly.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I'll be checking around here. You and the others can start looking elsewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Asakawa
dialogues.text: Sorry, many of the items were moved here recently, so things are still a bit unorganized.

dialogues.speaker: Asakawa
dialogues.text: Although the previous warehouse was large, the locks were dated, and something was nearly stolen. So, Madam Kujou Sara ordered the contents to be moved here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kazuha said he would wait for us at The Five Kasen Plaza today. Let's go find him there.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Everyone, I've found something that you should all have a look at.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Seems Kazuha discovered something, let's go see what he's got!
